20261124-fe45819a-a1.description:
Nestled in the arid hills of western Thebes over three thousand years ago lay Set Ma’at, meaning The Place of Truth. Known today as Deir el-Medina, this secluded desert village was home to the royal stonecutters, sculptors, draughtsmen, and scribes who carved and painted the magnificent tombs in the Valley of the Kings.

Away from the grand monuments of the pharaohs, these specialized artisans led remarkably structured daily lives. From eight-day work shifts inside subterranean tombs to domestic squabbles, legal rights for women, and history's first recorded labor strike over delayed grain rations, explore what life was truly like for the ordinary people behind ancient Egypt's eternal wonders.
